# Backtest: pre-match win probability

Chronological replay of 257,738 singles matches (TML-Database 1968–Jan 2026, API-Tennis ATP after that and Challenger/qualifying from 2019), of which 199,081 are tour-level main draw and are the only ones scored. Each match is predicted from ratings that have absorbed only earlier matches, then it updates them. Model choices were made on **2014-01-01 – 2018-12-31** (validation) and scored on **2019-01-01 – 2026-01-21** (test). The **forward** window (2026-01-22 on) is API-Tennis data that no choice ever saw.

Excluded from both rating updates and scoring: walkovers, defaults, unknown results, and every row whose player identity failed a check (ID/name conflict, unknown or missing ID, placeholder player).

## Data decision: Challenger and qualifying results

API-Tennis adds Challenger and qualifying matches from 2019. They update ratings but are never scored. Whether to use them was decided on 2021–22 tour matches (where that data exists); 2023 on and the forward window were not used for the choice. Chosen: **with_challenger_k1.5_qualifying_k0.25**.

## Scorelines: straight sets and tiebreaks

The Markov chain also predicts how a match is won. Its point probabilities are anchored so that its match-win chance equals the served model's (the serve/return ratings set how serve-dominated the matchup is). Checked against actual scores (completed matches):

| Window | n | Straight sets, predicted | observed | log loss | Tiebreaks per match, chain | calibrated | observed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| validation | 14,180 | 0.590 | 0.605 | 0.6593 | 0.526 | 0.488 | 0.488 |
| test | 18,438 | 0.588 | 0.605 | 0.6527 | 0.522 | 0.484 | 0.481 |
| forward | 2,465 | 0.590 | 0.600 | 0.6571 | 0.536 | 0.497 | 0.509 |
| serve_return_only_test | 18,438 | 0.604 | 0.605 | 0.6569 | 0.505 | – | 0.481 |
| independent_points_test | 18,438 | 0.553 | 0.605 | 0.6705 | 0.560 | – | 0.481 |

Match-level form on the day (sd 0.15 on the logit scale, chosen on validation straight-sets log loss plus the tiebreak count's Poisson likelihood) is what brings these into line: with independent points the chain predicts too few straight sets and too many tiebreaks. `serve_return_only_test` is the same chain without the anchor. The calibrated tiebreak count multiplies the chain's by 0.927, fitted on validation (so validation matches by construction).

## Context features on top of the served model

Greedy selection on validation of a logistic layer over the served probability. Candidates (see `features.py`): player differences `age`, `lefty`, `h2h`, `rest`, `load`, `home`, `exp`, `switch`, `travel`; and context terms that rescale the served logit, `conf`, `bo5`, `indoor`, `clay`, `grass`, `slam`, `masters`, `late`. Selected: `age`, `exp`, `rest`, `conf`, `indoor`, `bo5`, `h2h`, `load`.

## Walk-forward refit of the context layer

The layer's weights refit each January on the previous years only, against weights fixed on 2014–15. Decided on 2016–18: fixed 0.5914, yearly refit 1-year window 0.5915, 2-year window 0.5910, 3-year window 0.5911. Adopted (2-year window).

| Window | n | Weights fixed on validation | Yearly refit | Gain ± se |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| test | 18,937 | 0.5994 | 0.5997 | -0.0003 ± 0.0004 |
| test_2023_on | 9,165 | 0.6020 | 0.6019 | 0.0000 ± 0.0007 |
| forward | 2,521 | 0.5994 | 0.5971 | 0.0024 ± 0.0008 |

Lower is better for Brier, log loss and ECE (expected calibration error, 10 bins). Market comparison: see `docs/markets.md`.

Selected Elo, completed matches only (retirements removed): Brier 0.2114, log loss 0.6088, n = 18,438.

Serving model, chosen by validation log loss among the last three rows: **walk_forward**. Blend: logit p = 0.588 × logit p_Elo + 0.273 × logit p_Markov (coefficients fitted on validation; the blend's validation score is therefore slightly optimistic).

Blend vs selected Elo on the same test matches (positive = blend better): brier gain 0.0028 ± 0.0003 (z = 8.2); log_loss gain 0.0065 ± 0.0008 (z = 8.2).

## Serve/return model

Each player has serve and return ratings on the logit scale; P(A wins a point on serve) = sigmoid(surface average + serve_A − return_B). Each match's serve points won update the ratings by a one-step Bayesian (Laplace) step, so players with few stat lines stay near the pool. The point probabilities go through a game → tiebreak → set → match Markov chain with each event's deciding-set rules (advantage sets, 12–12 and 10-point tiebreaks by Slam and year). Matches without a valid stat line still get a prediction but do not update the ratings.

Prior and drift variances are chosen on the **blend's** validation log loss, because the blend is what is served; per-player surface offsets are then added only if they improve it further (they did).

## How the Elo model was chosen

Greedy forward selection: start from the FiveThirtyEight-style blend, try each single change, adopt the one that most improves **validation** log loss, repeat until nothing improves. Test numbers are shown for transparency only; they played no part in the choice.

| Step | Validation log loss | Test log loss | Test Brier | Test ECE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline (FiveThirtyEight-style blend) | 0.60074 | 0.63429 | 0.22141 | 0.0540 |
| + prediction scale x1.3 | 0.59587 | 0.62514 | 0.21836 | 0.0187 |
| + margin of victory, squared | 0.59350 | 0.62491 | 0.21808 | 0.0280 |
| + best-of-5 adjustment | 0.59283 | 0.62549 | 0.21825 | 0.0347 |
| + merge indoor hard into hard | 0.59266 | 0.62520 | 0.21800 | 0.0369 |

Selected configuration: `surface_weight=0.5`, `split_indoor_hard=False`, `new_player_prior=flat`, `surface_init=flat`, `bo5_adjust=True`, `pred_scale=1.3`, `k_num=250.0`, `k_offset=5.0`, `k_shape=0.4`.
